info.title: hexaeight-activate — HexaEight identity activation CLI
info.description: Command-line tool for HexaEight identities on this machine: install the official agent (downloaded from GitHub and hash-verified against a value shipped inside this package), activate a machine token, renew it, verify the licence, check that the HexaEight libraries an agent is running match the packages published on nuget.org, and control which agent builds an identity accepts messages from. Subcommands: install-agent, install-router, install-workspace, install-examples, upstreams (provider routes and keys), models (ask a provider what it serves), engine (point an engine at a route), restart, update, autostart, newtoken (default), renewtoken, cpucores, verify-env, verify-libs, approve-builds. `engine --validate` repairs engines sealed with an out-of-date priming, in place, without re-asking for a route or model.

commands.name: autostart
commands.description:
Start router, then agent, then workspace at login — in that
order, each waiting for the previous one to answer.
on | off

commands.name: cpucores
commands.description:
Print the CPU and core count this machine reports.
Your HexaEight license must cover at least this many cores.

commands.name: engine
commands.description:
Which ROUTE an engine asks for, and which env vars carry it.
Asks four things and writes the sealed engine entry through
the agent: what the engine speaks (Claude / OpenAI / Codex /
custom), the route, the provider's own model id, and the
router's agent name.
The model field ends up as  <route>|<model>  — the router
globs the left half to pick an upstream and sends the right
half to the provider, so a route name never has to be a real
model id.
Run it from the identity folder. If upstreams.yaml is here the
routes are listed and checked; if the router is on another
machine they are simply asked for.
--dir PATH  the identity folder to seal into

commands.name: help
commands.description: Show this message.

commands.name: install-examples
commands.description:
Put a small local model on this machine, point the agent at
it, and write runnable examples. No API key and no account —
it exists so a fresh install can do something immediately.
Not for production; bring a provider key for real work.
--dir PATH      install somewhere other than here
--model-only    skip the example files

commands.name: install-router
commands.description:
Download the official LLM router for this platform and
verify it. The router fronts your model providers, so the
agents calling it never hold a provider key.
--dir PATH  install somewhere other than the current folder

commands.name: install-workspace
commands.description:
Download the prebuilt workspace UI and extract it.
--agent NAME  which agent this workspace signs in to. Naming
one implies the browser is NOT on its machine,
so the agent is reached by its public URL from
the registry. Applies without --force.
--local       browser IS on the agent's machine (the default)
--remote      it is not, without naming an agent
--force       replace an existing install
--dir PATH    install somewhere other than here

commands.name: models
commands.description:
Ask each configured provider what models it will serve, using the
key already in upstreams.yaml. The model id is the one part of
the wiring that cannot be guessed — and a 401/403 here is the
cheapest way to find out a key has expired.
--filter TEXT  only ids containing TEXT
--tag TAG      only routes ending -TAG
--dir PATH     a router in another folder

commands.name: newtoken
commands.description:
Interactive activation (default if no command is given).
Prompts for resource name, password, license code,
and a QR-code approval from the HexaEight Authenticator app.
Writes env-file and hexaeight.mac to the current directory.
On success, runs a quick license verification automatically.

commands.name: Notes
commands.description:
- Run from the directory where you want env-file and hexaeight.mac
to be written (typically your application's working directory).
- For the Azure Marketplace VM activation path, see the docs at
hexaeight.com/docs.

commands.name: renewtoken
commands.description:
Renew an existing license. Prompts for the new
license code received by email after purchase.
Updates HEXAEIGHT_MACHINETOKEN in env-file.
On success, runs a quick license verification automatically.

commands.name: restart
commands.description:
Restart a component: agent (with Node-RED), workspace, router,
or router-then-agent. The UI needs only a browser refresh.

commands.name: sandbox
commands.description:
Can turns be confined on this machine, and does the sandbox
actually RUN? Linux needs bubblewrap (a sudo install, reported
here rather than done for you); macOS uses sandbox-exec, which
is part of the OS; Windows has no backend.
Present-but-broken is the state that matters: the agent picks
its backend by existence, so a sandbox that cannot run takes
every turn down with it.

commands.name: stop
commands.description:
Stop a component and leave it stopped.
agent       the daemon and every process it spawned
router      note: an agent holding routes into it then
fails its next turn with a model error
workspace   the UI server
all         workspace, then agent, then router
Tunnels are left alone. With NO component named this still
disables the local qwen model — what bare `stop` has always
meant.

commands.name: update
commands.description: Replace one component and restart only that component.

commands.name: upstreams
commands.description:
Which PROVIDERS this router can reach. Pick from a list and
paste one key per provider; the URLs are not guessable, so
they are chosen rather than typed.
Routes are named  *-<dialect>-<tag>  — dialect is ant|oai|res
(the API the caller speaks), tag is one provider AND one key.
--list                 show what is configured
--migrate              convert older route names, backing
the file up first
--migrate --keep-old   convert, and leave the previous names
working so engines can move one at a
time
--dir PATH             a router in another folder

commands.name: verify-env
commands.description:
Run a license verification — encrypt and decrypt a random
probe message locally to confirm the activation is healthy.
Then check the agent's libraries, as verify-libs does.

options.name: --restore
options.description: replace any that do not match

options.name: --dir
options.description:
check a specific folder
Exit: 0 all match, 1 a mismatch, 2 nothing found to check.
